Vidushi Toshniwal

Department of Geoscience and Geo-Engineering · TU Delft, NL

I am pursuing my Ph.D. under the supervision of Prof. Dr. Michael Hicks, Dr.ir. Wout Broere, and Dr.ir. Anne-Catherine Dieudonné. My research focuses on geomechanics, particularly the time-dependent hydro-mechanical behavior of geomaterials in context of deep geological disposal of high-level radioactive waste.

My research interests lie at the intersection of computational methods and experimental soil behavior, with practical applications. I have gained valuable research experiences at Purdue University and Rowan University in the USA and Leibniz University, Hannover, DE. I have also been fortunate to gain industry experience through internship at Schlumberger, India.

I come from Kota, a city widely known as an education hub in India. My academic journey began with a dual degree from IIT Delhi with bachelors in Civil engineering and masters in Geotechnical and Geo-environmental engineering. My master's thesis focused on study of offshore monopile foundations behavior under cyclic loading.

Projects

Time-dependent hydro-mechanical behaviour of clays in context of deep geological disposal

PhD project, TU Delft
  • NWO funded research project to study coupled hydro-mechanical behaviour of representative clay samples from deep Neogene and Paleogene clay formations from the Dutch subsurface.
  • Performed detailed characterisation of clay cores obtained and analysing experimental behaviour under 1D consolidation and triaxial conditions at high stress levels.
September 2023 - Present

GIS based Geotechnical Database for Collaborative GIS

Research Assistant, Purdue University
  • Developed a GIS-based geotechnical database for the Indiana Department of Transportation (INDOT) to facilitate collaborative GIS and improve data accessibility.
  • Designed classes to abstract project details and developed relations between them to enable rich and complex queries.
August 2022- April 2023

Analysing offshore foundations under cyclic loading in clay

Master thesis project, IIT Delhi and LUH, DE
  • Project shortlisted for DAAD fellowship, analysing monopile foundations behaviour, evaluating existing p-y approaches.
  • Finite element analysis on PLAXIS 3D using UDCAM-s soil models; formulated equations for cyclic displacement degradation for millions of load cycles and validated results with the field tests available.
August 2021 - July 2022

Noninvasive 3D imaging and characterization of permafrost profiles

Research internship, Rowan University, USA
  • Studied relationship between electrical resistivity of frozen soil and key parameters for permafrost characterization.
  • Conceptualised and performed lab-scale 1D electrical resistivity measurements of frost-susceptible clayey sands, focusing on major influencing factors including initial water content, soil density, temperature, freezing-thawing.
January 2020 - March 2020

Analysis of behaviour of deep excavations

Bachelor thesis project, IIT Delhi
  • Finite Element Modeling and simulation of behaviour of underground retaining walls under dynamic loading.
  • Studied the existing design parameters and analysed the improvements required to make them earthquake resistant.
  • Achieved 33.33% decrease in deformation by anchored wall, performed parametric analysis by varying the properties.
July 2019 - November 2019

Ground improvement by nanomaterials inclusion

Summer Undergraduate Research Project, IIT Delhi
  • Assessed feasibility of using commercially available stabilizers to prevent damages in clay, analysed literature.
  • Reduced volumetric strains and crack intensity factor by conducting 13 tests on bentonite clay with TerraSil.
May 2018 - January 2019
